macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Treasury yields surge as oil rises and U.S.-Iran tensions hit risk appetite
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields climbed on Tuesday, with the 30-year yield rising to around 5.322% and the 10-year at 4.736%, as investors reacted to higher oil prices and persistent U.S.-Iran tensions. The move reflects renewed pressure on bonds and broader risk assets over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Global equities soften as bond yields rise and risk-off sentiment builds
items.summary: Markets traded weaker as higher long-term Treasury yields and geopolitical concerns weighed on sentiment, with U.S. stock futures and global equities under pressure. Newsquawk reported that the U.S. 30-year yield near 5.32% helped drive a softer tone across risk assets.

items.title: ECB’s Lane says inflation may remain near 3% for the rest of the year
items.summary: European Central Bank policymaker Philip Lane said inflation is expected to hover around 3% for the rest of the year, though he tied that outlook to whether the current crisis is resolved. The comments underscore a still-cautious central bank backdrop.

items.title: Fed outlook remains in focus after recent rate cut and signal for one more in 2026
items.summary: Investor attention remains on the Federal Reserve after it cut its key interest rate and signaled one more cut in 2026. This remains one of the key macro policy developments shaping rate expectations.

items.title: U.S. retail sales fell 0.6% in July, adding to evidence of slower consumer demand
items.summary: Retail sales declined 0.6% in July from the prior month, marking the steepest drop since May 2025. The data points to softer consumer spending momentum heading into the latest trading session.

items.title: Annual U.S. inflation slowed to 3.4% in July
items.summary: BBC Business reported that U.S. inflation cooled for a second straight month, easing to 3.4% in July. The figure is important for interest-rate expectations and the broader macro backdrop.

items.title: Chip stocks rise on renewed confidence in AI spending
items.summary: MarketWatch reported that Micron, Sandisk and other chip stocks climbed as investors grew more confident about AI-related spending. The move highlights continued strength in the semiconductor trade despite broader market volatility.

items.title: FTSE 100 slips as oil climbs and bonds stay under pressure
items.summary: Bloomberg’s live markets coverage said Brent crude moved back above $91, helping support energy names while keeping the broader FTSE 100 under pressure. The report ties the move to a broader risk-off mood across markets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP post mixed 24-hour moves as BTC rebounds near $64K
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around the mid-$60,000 range over the past day, with one market recap putting BTC up 2% to about $64,260 while Ethereum rose 1.3% and XRP was flat to slightly higher. Another report said BTC hovered near $62,905 with ETH, XRP, and SOL slightly lower, underscoring continued volatility across major tokens.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs toward $64,000 on cooling inflation and lower Treasury yields
items.summary: A market update said Bitcoin rose 1.44% in 24 hours and Ethereum gained 0.43% as softer inflation and falling Treasury yields supported a broader recovery in crypto prices. The report framed the move as a macro-driven rebound after recent pressure.

items.title: South Korea orders Polymarket block over gambling concerns
items.summary: South Korean authorities ordered a block on Polymarket, citing illegal gambling concerns. The move adds to growing regulatory pressure on prediction-market and crypto-linked platforms.

items.title: EU opens door to country-wide crypto bans tied to Russia sanctions evasion
items.summary: European authorities signaled that member states could impose broader crypto restrictions when needed to address Russia sanctions evasion. The report points to a possible tightening of enforcement around digital assets in the EU.

items.title: China adds 8 banks to digital yuan network
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that China expanded its digital yuan infrastructure by adding eight banks, bringing the network operator count to 30. The development indicates continued state-led progress in China’s central bank digital currency rollout.

items.title: Tether completes first-ever audit
items.summary: A crypto market recap said Tether achieved a milestone by completing its first independent audit. The same report also noted related market and regulatory headlines, including SEC and banking developments affecting the crypto sector.

items.title: SEC cancels vote on capital-raising exemptions for crypto startups
items.summary: According to a market recap, the SEC canceled a planned vote on capital-raising exemptions for crypto startups. The delay keeps uncertainty in place for early-stage crypto fundraising and token issuance structures.

items.title: OCC conditionally approves bank charter for World Liberty Financial
items.summary: A market recap said the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency conditionally approved a bank charter for World Liberty Financial, a Trump-linked crypto venture. The approval is a notable institutional development for a politically connected crypto project.

items.title: Binance plans FCA application in the UK
items.summary: The latest market roundup said Binance is preparing an application with the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority. The move suggests the exchange is seeking a more formal regulatory foothold in one of its key markets.

items.title: JPMorgan cuts ties with Polymarket over regulatory concerns
items.summary: A market recap reported that JPMorgan ended its relationship with Polymarket due to regulatory concerns. The decision highlights how compliance risk is affecting access to traditional banking services for crypto and prediction-market firms.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 3.7 Flash, a new model released just three weeks after the previous version, signaling a faster release cadence in its AI lineup.

items.title: OpenAI signs major Ohio data center lease with Nvidia backing
items.summary: OpenAI has locked in a lease for a large data center in Ohio, with Nvidia reported to be providing support for the project as the company expands its infrastructure footprint.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly scales back plans for OpenAI data center funding guarantee
items.summary: Reports indicate Nvidia downsized its planned guarantee for a $250 billion OpenAI data center effort, highlighting shifting financing dynamics in AI infrastructure.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Glimmer open-weight model
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Glimmer, described as an open-weight model aimed at local coding, agentic tasks, and multi-step reasoning, continuing its push toward open AI models.

items.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 Sol ultrafast mode
items.summary: OpenAI launched an ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, claiming up to 14x faster processing for users who need lower-latency responses.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6-Cyber for cybersecurity
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-5.6-Cyber through Daybreak, positioning the model for stronger cyber defense and security-related workflows.

items.title: Anthropic adds hidden watermarks to Claude text
items.summary: Anthropic is adding hidden watermarks to Claude-generated text to make AI-generated content easier to identify, reflecting growing emphasis on provenance and trust.

items.title: Microsoft merges Copilot apps and retires several AI tools
items.summary: Microsoft is consolidating Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot into a single app while retiring multiple AI-powered tools, indicating a product simplification move.

items.title: Spotify to label AI-generated artist profiles
items.summary: Spotify plans to add a new AI persona badge to identify AI-generated artist profiles, part of a broader industry push to label synthetic content.

items.title: Razorpay launches Vulcan AI model for payments
items.summary: Razorpay unveiled Vulcan, an AI model trained on 4 billion payments, showing continued adoption of domain-specific AI systems in fintech.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony and S-GAME confirm a deep dive on Phantom Blade Zero
items.summary: Sony confirmed a State of Play deep dive for Phantom Blade Zero, with the presentation expected to air across the late evening or early morning depending on time zone. The announcement adds fresh momentum for one of PlayStation’s most closely watched upcoming action games.

items.title: Valve updates AI disclosure rules for Steam
items.summary: GameSpot reports that Valve has updated its AI disclosure guidelines to allow AI-powered tools under its platform rules. The change is significant for developers as it clarifies how generative AI and other AI-assisted workflows can be used on Steam.

items.title: Netflix is closing two game studios
items.summary: The Verge reports that Netflix is shutting down two of its game studios, signaling another shift in the company’s gaming strategy. The move is part of ongoing changes to Netflix’s broader push into games.

items.title: A Senate subcommittee opens an investigation into Roblox child safety
items.summary: The Verge reports that a Senate subcommittee has opened an investigation into Roblox over child safety concerns. The probe highlights intensifying scrutiny of the platform’s moderation and protections for younger users.

items.title: Warren Spector announces his retirement from game development
items.summary: GamesRadar and Gamereactor report that Warren Spector, known for Deus Ex and System Shock, is retiring after 44 years in the industry. His departure marks the end of a long career that helped shape immersive sim design.

items.title: The Sims 4 receives a free update ahead of the next expansion
items.summary: Eurogamer reports that The Sims 4 has added glass walls, rooftop greenery, inventory improvements, and other free content ahead of its next expansion. The update gives players new building options and quality-of-life features.

items.title: Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter rolls out a legacy patch
items.summary: Nintendo Life reports that Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter received a legacy patch, with full details now available. The update appears to address post-launch support and compatibility improvements.

items.title: Simpsons creator Matt Groening appears to hint at a Hit & Run remaster
items.summary: VGC and PC Gamer report that Matt Groening seemingly implied a remaster or return of The Simpsons Hit & Run, though the show’s current showrunner quickly disputed the idea. The situation has fueled new speculation around the cult classic game.

items.title: Esports Nations Cup delayed to 2027
items.summary: Gamereactor reports that the Esports Nations Cup has been pushed from November 2026 to November 2027 because of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The delay is a notable setback for the international esports event calendar.

items.title: Game industry layoffs remain a major concern in 2026
items.summary: 18183 reports that the game industry has averaged 44 job losses per day so far in 2026, underscoring continued staffing pressure across the sector. The report reflects ongoing restructuring and contraction in parts of the industry.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: OpenAI secures huge Ohio data-center lease with Nvidia backing
items.summary: OpenAI has locked in a lease for a large Ohio data-center project, with Nvidia reportedly providing major financial support. The deal underscores the continuing race to secure massive computing infrastructure for tech platforms and cloud workloads.

items.title: Nvidia commits up to $105 billion in financing for OpenAI’s Ohio project
items.summary: Nvidia is reported to be providing up to $105 billion in backing for OpenAI’s Ohio data-center development, one of the largest infrastructure commitments in the current tech cycle. The project is expected to support large-scale computing capacity for future products and services.

items.title: YouTube changes how it counts video views
items.summary: YouTube will now count a view as soon as a video starts playing, instead of waiting for roughly 30 seconds of watch time. The change could significantly affect view counts across the platform.

items.title: Apple accidentally confirms camera-equipped AirPods are coming
items.summary: Apple appears to have inadvertently confirmed that AirPods with built-in cameras are in development. If launched, the product would expand Apple’s wearable line beyond audio-focused features.

items.title: Starlink’s new gigabit gateways draw interference complaint from Iridium
items.summary: Starlink’s new gigabit gateway deployment has triggered an interference complaint from Iridium. The dispute highlights ongoing spectrum and coexistence tensions in satellite communications.

items.title: Uber targets 1 million drone deliveries per day by 2029
items.summary: Uber says it aims to scale drone deliveries to 1 million per day by 2029. The plan signals a major push into autonomous logistics and last-mile delivery technology.

items.title: Windows Defender flaw could let attackers escalate privileges
items.summary: Security researchers identified the ‘ShieldBreak’ flaw, which could allow an attacker to use Windows Defender to gain elevated privileges on a Windows system. The issue adds to ongoing concerns about endpoint security in enterprise environments.

items.title: Meta faces a major child-privacy trial
items.summary: Meta is heading into a high-stakes legal trial that could reshape how Facebook and Instagram handle child privacy and safety issues. The case is among the most significant non-AI tech company developments in the past day.
